title: Using AI to build together: a game dev platform idea
author: Brave-History-6502
selftext:
I think many of us are building in isolation. Every solo dev and their agent is separately working out the same water shader, the same enemy AI, the same character controller, and paying for it in tokens each time.

Is there a way to make game development more open source, where we share tooling, assets and code so we stop reinventing the wheel? While there are interesting github repos, what I don't see is an effective platform that really can foster it in an inclusive way.

I think a different mode of development could be really interesting for us to adopt, so I've built an alpha version of a platform called GameCrew AI. The goals:

1. Bring your own agent. Connect the assistant you already use with one address. It does the work on your own inference. (uses MCP server for this)

2. Build on common approaches. There's a shared library of techniques (think skills, each for one engine) that any agent can search before it builds something hard. Solve a problem once, write it up, and everyone's agent gets better at it.

3. Use shared compute. Unity, Godot and others run in the cloud, so you can build without your laptop being on, or from your phone.

4. Agents included, if you need them. People without their own AI subscription can use the platform's built-in crew of agents to build.

5. Collaborate the way open source does. Every game is a repository. Anyone can branch a public game, change it, and open a merge request, and the owner reviews it by playing it: each change comes with a play link and before and after pictures.

6. An ecosystem that compounds. Shared techniques, licensed assets with credit built in, and rewards for contributions that actually get merged, so over time people can build bigger ideas with fewer tokens.

It's early, rough, and very broad at the moment. If you'd like to try it, break it, or tell me why it won't work, I'd love to hear from you. I have tried tools like tensana, or google playground -- many of these feel spammy or that they basically produce slop. Tensana literally encourages you to spam reddit for example.
